item.title: Battery Fire at Sixth Street SRO Sends One Resident to the Hospital
item.description: There was a large fire department and police response near Sixth and Market streets Wednesday night, which stemmed from a fire inside an SRO unit.

item.title: Trump Fires Kristi Noem and Installs New Clown to Lead Homeland Security
item.description: Given Trump's well established penchant for firing people, going a full year in office without a high-profile firing says something. But now Kristi Noem, aka ICE Barbie, the underqualified and always out-of-her-depth Secretary of Homeland Security, is out.

item.title: Two Stabbed In Dolores Park Altercation Wednesday, Multiple Teens In Custody
item.description: SFPD confronted a “group of unknown subjects in a physical altercation” at Mission Dolores Park Wednesday afternoon, and more disturbingly, six of the eight suspects arrested were teens.

item.title: It Will Likely Be a Year Before the Port of SF's Sinking Dry Dock #2 Can Be Demolished and Removed
item.description: The Port of San Francisco is reportedly crossing its collective fingers that the massive, listing Dry Dock #2, which currently requires constant pumping to keep it from sinking, doesn't sink to the bottom of the Bay before they can remove it, a process that isn't likely to happen before next winter.

item.title: The Big Four Makes Big Return This Month on Nob Hill at the Revamped Huntington Hotel
item.description: As we were getting periodic news in recent months about the reopening of the 104-year-old Huntington Hotel, the big question for those of us who won't be booking thousand-dollar rooms there has been when the moody restaurant and lounge known as The Big Four would be back open.

item.title: BART Police Rocked by Racist AI Deepfake Video Being Texted Around Among Ranks
item.description: What is it with Bay Area law enforcement and their racist text messages? Yet another such scandal just hit the BART Police force, in a video where BART Police officers singled out a Sikh colleague for mockery.

item.title: Vigilante 'Squatter Removal' Guy Faces Assault and False Imprisonment Charges In San Mateo County
item.description: A self-described, extra-legal "squatter removal service" was allegedly being run by a sword-wielding, San Francisco-based guy who, along with two associates, now faces assault, burglary, and false imprisonment charges in San Mateo County.

item.title: Oakland’s Big Alysa Liu Victory Celebration Now Scheduled for Thursday, March 12
item.description: Oakland’s Alysa Liu victory celebration will not quite be a parade down Grand Avenue, but instead a rally on the steps of City Hall, and it's scheduled for 12 noon on Thursday, March 12

item.title: 'Paranormal Activity' Brings Jump-Scares and Spooky Vibes to the Stage at ACT
item.description: A stage play inspired by the Paranormal Activity film franchise arrived at San Francisco's ACT in recent weeks, and it could presage a new paradigm for the horror genre coming to the live theater.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: Airbnb Settles $120 Million Lawsuit Against SF For Exactly $0
item.description: Sheng Thao’s lawyers had a bad day in court; our military actions against Iran are raising gas prices and pummeling the stock market; and Airbnb is giving up on getting $120 million back from the City of San Francisco.
